newsitem.title: USA: Seneca participated in 2 successful wells.
newsitem.headline: Seneca participated in 2 successful wells.

text.p: Seneca Resources Corp said Tuesday it participated in two successful wells on the outer continental shelf of the Gulf of Mexico.
The National Fuel Gas Co subsidiary also said it has reached an early payout of costs to explore and develop Vermilion Block 252.
The payout came about six months ahead of the projected payout date and was primarily due to lower than expected project and operating costs along with higher oil and gas prices.

Seneca earned operating rights in this property through a farmout from a third party which has elected to convert its override to a 35 percent working interest. Seneca said it will continue to operate and own the remaining 65 percent.
On High Island Block 194, located offshore Texas, production started on March 1 from the OCS-G 0616 Nos. JA-2 and JA-3 wells, operated by Shell Offshore Inc.

The JA-2 is producing 6 million cubic feet of natural gas and 46 barrels of condensate per day. The JA-3 encountered 3 pay zones totaling 99 net feet and was completed in the deepest zone. It is producing 11.5 million cubic feet of natural gas and 62 barrels of condensate per day. The Royal Dutch/Shell Group's subsidiary owns a 45 percent interest, Seneca 55 percent, it said.

Offshore Louisiana in OCS waters, the OCS-G 15062 Well 1, located in West Cameron Block 182 was drilled to a 12,600 feet, encountering 87 net feet of gas sand in three separate zones. The well was completed in the deepest zone and placed on production March 26 at the rate of 10 million cubic feet of natural gas and 60 barrels of condensate per day.
The well is presently cleaning up, Seneca said.

A second well drilled failed to encounter the productive sands found in the discovery well and was plugged and abandoned. Seneca operates and owns 66.67 percent working interest in the producing well and the lease. Shell Offshore owns the remaining 33.33 percent interest.
